aliases.title: Software Developer
aliases.scope_finding: The target's official definition (research, design and develop computer and network software; analyse user needs; enhance existing software) is what the market title names. SOC separates programmers, QA testers and web developers into their own occupations, so those are neighbours, not alternatives for this title.
aliases.overbroad_risk: low: market usage sometimes includes web developers or programmers, which SOC classifies separately; the alias maps only to the SOC-defined occupation.

target_detail.definition_excerpt: Research, design, and develop computer and network software or specialized utility programs. aliases.title: Human Resources Manager
aliases.scope_finding: The definition (plan, direct or coordinate human resources activities and staff) matches the market title; the definition itself excludes the specialised compensation-and-benefits and training-and-development managers, which keep their own codes.
aliases.overbroad_risk: low: a specialised HR manager is a SOC neighbour, not covered by this alias.

target_detail.label: Human Resources Managers
target_detail.definition_excerpt: Plan, direct, or coordinate human resources activities and staff of an organization. Excludes managers who primarily focus on compensation and benefits (11-3111) and training and development (11-3131).

competing_detail.label: Compensation and Benefits Managers
competing_detail.definition_excerpt: Plan, direct, or coordinate compensation and benefits activities of an organization. Job analysis and position description managers are included in “Human Resources Managers” (11-3121).

competing_detail.label: Training and Development Managers
competing_detail.definition_excerpt: Plan, direct, or coordinate the training and development activities and staff of an organization.

competing_detail.label: General and Operations Managers

aliases.title: Sales Manager
aliases.scope_finding: The definition (plan, direct or coordinate distribution of a product or service to the customer; sales territories, quotas and goals; training sales representatives) matches the market title. Marketing managers and first-line sales supervisors are separate occupations.
aliases.overbroad_risk: low to moderate: informal use of the title for first-line sales supervisors falls under 41-1011 and 41-1012.

target_detail.label: Sales Managers
target_detail.definition_excerpt: Plan, direct, or coordinate the actual distribution or movement of a product or service to the customer. Coordinate sales distribution by establishing sales territories, quotas, and goals and establish training programs for sales representatives. Analyze sales statistics gathered by staff to determine sales potential and inventory requirements and monitor the preferences of customers.

competing_detail.label: First-Line Supervisors of Retail Sales Workers

aliases.title: Accountant
aliases.scope_finding: SOC publishes ONE occupation, Accountants and Auditors, whose definition covers preparing financial statements and auditing statements prepared by others. The market title is narrower than the occupation, and the wage statistic describes the combined occupation. Tax preparers and bookkeeping clerks are separate occupations.
aliases.overbroad_risk: moderate: a salary shown for 'Accountant' is the combined Accountants and Auditors statistic.
conditions: every answer must carry the scope caveat that the figure is for Accountants and Auditors combined (implemented through the alias limitation text)

target_detail.label: Accountants and Auditors
target_detail.definition_excerpt: Examine, analyze, and interpret accounting records to prepare financial statements, give advice, or audit and evaluate statements prepared by others. Install or advise on systems of recording costs or other financial and budgetary data. Excludes “Tax Examiners and Collectors, and Revenue Agents” (13-2081).

competing_detail.label: Tax Preparers
competing_detail.definition_excerpt: Prepare tax returns for individuals or small businesses. Excludes “Accountants and Auditors” (13-2011).

competing_detail.label: Tax Examiners and Collectors, and Revenue Agents
competing_detail.definition_excerpt: Determine tax liability or collect taxes from individuals or business firms according to prescribed laws and regulations.

competing_detail.label: Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks

aliases.title: Financial Analyst
aliases.scope_finding: The official occupation is Financial and Investment Analysts: quantitative analyses of investment programs or financial data, including valuation. Its definition excludes budget analysts, financial risk specialists and securities sales agents, and credit analysts are a separate occupation. Market usage of 'financial analyst' spans those neighbours (for example corporate planning or credit work).
aliases.overbroad_risk: moderate to high: the title may refer to an adjacent SOC occupation depending on the employer function.
aliases.context_required: investment or valuation work (otherwise the occupation scope caveat applies)
conditions: every answer must carry the scope caveat naming Financial and Investment Analysts and the excluded neighbouring occupations
the reviewer decides whether the alias may be the default reading of the bare title or must require investment/valuation context; if neither is acceptable the title should be treated as ambiguous

target_detail.label: Financial and Investment Analysts
target_detail.definition_excerpt: Conduct quantitative analyses of information involving investment programs or financial data of public or private institutions, including valuation of businesses. Excludes “Budget Analysts” (13-2031), “Financial Risk Specialists” (13-2054), and “Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents” (41-3031).

competing_detail.label: Budget Analysts
competing_detail.definition_excerpt: Examine budget estimates for completeness, accuracy, and conformance with procedures and regulations. Analyze budgeting and accounting reports. Excludes “Financial and Investment Analysts” (13-2051).

competing_detail.label: Credit Analysts
competing_detail.definition_excerpt: Analyze credit data and financial statements of individuals or firms to determine the degree of risk involved in extending credit or lending money. Prepare reports with credit information for use in decisionmaking. Excludes “Financial Risk

competing_detail.label: Financial Risk Specialists
competing_detail.definition_excerpt: Analyze and measure exposure to credit and market risk threatening the assets, earning capacity, or economic state of an organization. May make recommendations to limit risk. Excludes “Credit Analysts” (13-2041).

competing_detail.label: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
competing_detail.definition_excerpt: Buy and sell securities or commodities in investment and trading firms, or provide financial services to businesses and individuals. May advise customers about stocks, bonds, mutual funds, commodities, and market conditions.

unresolved_titles.title: Data Analyst
unresolved_titles.finding: SOC 2018 has no occupation titled Data Analyst. Several occupations are defined around analysing data (data mining and modelling; statistical methods; mathematical optimisation; organisational studies; systems analysis; market research), and nothing in the approved sources says which one the market title denotes. A unique identity is not supported; a context-based identity would need the analyst's field, which is not known.
unresolved_titles.safe_behaviour: no alias; the resolver keeps returning not_found; a product contract could ask for occupational context, which is a product decision
unresolved_titles.needed_for_resolution: an approved occupational-title source that evidences the title, or candidate-supplied context plus an owner-approved ambiguity handling rule
